summary: Pin preservation failed during dedicated GPU pool scale-down, causing partial canary eviction and fallback to older model
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reported that during a scheduled downscale of their dedicated GPU pool, requests for a pinned model (lumina-bert-v2.3-pin-2026-03) started returning responses from the older v2.2 model for ~20% of requests. The customer had pinned v2.3 at the route level for a canary rollout (10% weight), expecting only the canary traffic to hit v2.3. Instead, roughly a subset of pinned sessions were routed to v2.2 intermittently.

Impact:
- Customer-facing: Mixed model outputs caused data quality regressions in two production features (document tagging and entity extraction) for LuminaAnalytics customers.
- Scope: Affected ~15k requests over a 45 minute window in prod-us-east.
- Business: Lumina flagged as P1 due to incorrect data for paid customers on dedicated capacity.

Environment:
- Dedicated GPU pool (reserved) in us-east; autoscaler configured to downscale at 03:00 UTC with graceful drain timeout 300s.
- Route config: route_id=lumina/entity-extract, model_pin=lumina-bert-v2.3-pin-2026-03, canary_weight=0.10.
- Serving runtime version: 1.21.4; autoscaler version: 0.9.8.

Steps to reproduce (as observed by customer):
1. Lumina triggered a routine scheduled downscale at 03:00 UTC.
2. Within ~3 minutes, some pinned sessions began returning v2.2 outputs (no explicit unpin request from customer).
3. Attempts to re-pin via API returned 200 but client continued to see mixed outputs until routing cache was flushed 40 minutes later.

Logs and evidence:
- Router traces: http://dashboards.redwood/internal/routing-traces?trace=SUP-27458 (shows fallbacks from pins to default group)
- Autoscaler events: scale-down triggered; nodes marked for drain then marked unhealthy while EVP drain state still present: autoscaler logs snippet: "node-cc-17 drain_started=2026-03-10T03:01:02Z drain_complete=\"\""
- Serving logs (example): "[2026-03-10T03:03:12Z] route lumina/entity-extract: session 0x7f3 pinned_model=lumina-bert-v2.3 but routed_model=lumina-bert-v2.2 fallback_reason=pin-owner-unavailable"

Initial hypothesis:
- During scale-down, nodes that were draining moved to a transient unhealthy state. The routing layer treats the pin owner as unavailable when the node health is not yet marked drained, triggering fallback routing to the default model group. A race between drain and health-state transitions can therefore clear pin mappings for in-flight sessions.

Supporting observations:
- Traffic heatmap shows coincident increase in connection churn during node termination events.
- PKI: No TLS errors observed.
- No quota or rate-limit events recorded.

Recommended immediate mitigation (customer-facing workaround):
- Re-apply pin via API after scale-down completes (observed to fix most sessions).
- For scheduled downscales, increase graceful drain timeout to 600s as a temporary mitigation to reduce race window.

Longer-term fixes under consideration:
- Ensure pin ownership is decoupled from single-node health and validated across routing metadata layer before triggering fallback.
- Autoscaler change to mark node as "draining" in healthcheck path rather than immediate unhealthy.
- Add metrics and alerts for "pin-to-fallback" ratios during scale events.
investigation_notes: 03-10 04:00Z: Reviewed router and autoscaler logs; found multiple nodes transitioned from draining->unhealthy within 20-40s.
03-10 04:30Z: Reproduced locally on staging with forced node termination and confirmed routing falls back when pin-owner health shows unhealthy before drain completion.
Observed that the routing cache TTL (30s) allowed stale entries to be invalidated while drain still ongoing; when invalidated the fallback logic chooses default model group.
comments: Elena Martinez (Support) [2026-03-10T05:12Z]: Notified customer and collected request IDs and example responses; Lumina attached response samples showing v2.2 outputs.
Marcus Liu (SRE) [2026-03-10T06:01Z]: Started timeline correlation between autoscaler events and routing traces; suspect health-state transition order causes pin eviction.
Asha Patel (Platform Eng) [2026-03-10T08:20Z]: Created staging repro with forced termination; able to reproduce 2/5 runs. Filed PR to adjust health state semantics for draining nodes.
Lumina Support Rep (customer) [2026-03-10T09:05Z]: Confirmed re-applying pin fixed the immediate issue for active sessions; asked for ETA on permanent fix.

Marcus Liu (SRE) [2026-03-12T11:00Z]: Rolling a canary patch to autoscaler (PR #722) to mark draining nodes with health=draining; routing patch to tolerate draining nodes until drain_complete in PR #1867.
Elena Martinez (Support) [2026-03-12T12:15Z]: Updated customer on canary rollout and recommended increasing drain timeout as stop-gap.
resolution_notes: Mitigation applied: temporarily increased default graceful drain timeout for Lumina dedicated pool to 600s and re-applied pin mappings per their request. Engineering has deployed a canary autoscaler change (PR #722) in us-east with routing tolerance (PR #1867). Next steps: monitor pin-to-fallback metric for 48h, if stable schedule full rollout. Postmortem to be drafted if recurrence >1 in 7 days.
